key_insight: An LLM-based, retrieval-augmented system can simplify diabetes education materials into more patient-friendly language while keeping the content clinically grounded.
clinical_relevance: This could help patients better understand diabetes information, supporting clearer education and more informed decision-making.
method: Indexed diabetes resources from trusted sources such as Diabetes Australia, WHO, ADA, NIDDK, and AIHW.
Used RAG to retrieve relevant clinical information and an LLM to rewrite it in simpler language.
Evaluated output with readability metrics and a small human study.
evidence_signal: In the abstract, MediClear reduced reading level into the recommended patient literacy range and received high user satisfaction in a human evaluation with 10 participants.
watch_item: The human evaluation was small, so broader testing is needed before assuming the results generalize across patient groups and real-world settings.
paper_title: Medical Knowledge Simplification for Patients in the Era of LLMs: A Case Study on Diabetes
